endorsements.quote: Therefore, AI drafts should serve only as preliminary reports, awaiting radiologist confirmation.
The thoracic radiologists judged the tool to be suitable only for screening examinations reviewed by a radiologist.
The legal and ethical liabilities for patient harm must also be clarified before an autonomous operation is acceptable [ 19 ].
Conversely, the stand-alone use of AI-based tools in routine practice has been opposed.
Surveyed radiologists, therefore, emphasized expert-led education to minimize bias and prevent misuse.
Additional prospective studies are needed to confirm whether AI-generated reports improve reading accuracy and workflow efficiency.

unlisted_practices: Develop society-endorsed education and guidelines before adopting AI report-drafting tools.
Optimize AI report-drafting performance and validate it robustly in real-world settings before broader clinical adoption.
Do not share unvalidated AI-generated reports with non-radiologist medical personnel.
Restrict radiologists' exposure to AI drafts in health-screening and ICU settings to limit overreliance.

screen.reason: This is a professional society position statement and guideline from the Korean Society of Thoracic Radiology based on a Delphi consensus process evaluating automated chest X-ray report drafting.
